title: Crypto key provisioner Terraform wrapper for Vault + SecretsManager integration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a composable Terraform module (wrapper) that standardizes cryptographic key provisioning and secret onboarding across private VPC deployments. The module should provide an abstracted provider interface that supports AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, on-prem HSMs (CloudHSM-compatible or PKCS#11), and a Vault-backed key provider. It must implement safe lifecycle operations (create/rotate/decommission), IAM bindings for least privilege, and optional dual-write migrations between Secrets Manager and Vault. The wrapper will expose idempotent entry points for: key creation, aliasing, grant/policy attachment, secret bootstrap (Secrets Manager or Vault path), and automated rotation hooks. Operational requirements: drift detection alerts, a lightweight healthcheck lambda (or container) that verifies key status and secret sync, telemetry for rotate/failure events, and Terraform tests (terratest or kitchen-terraform) for each supported provider. The module should include upgrade compatibility paths (v1 -> v2) to allow rolling migration of keys/secrets with canary rotation and explicit rollback steps. Deliverables: Terraform module with examples, CI pipeline for acceptance tests, runbook for on-call and migration, and documentation in the private-deployments Confluence space.
acceptance_criteria: Module supports AWS KMS and Vault-backed keys with identical inputs/outputs
Healthcheck deployable in customer VPC and reports status to metrics/alerting
Automated integration tests pass for AWS and a mocked HSM provider in CI
Dual-write migration pattern documented and tested with a canary rotation
IAM policies generated by the module follow least-privilege templates
Module README with upgrade steps and known incompatibilities is published
riskiest_assumptions: Customers will permit a small healthcheck outbound telemetry endpoint for monitoring
On-prem HSM customers can expose a PKCS#11-compatible interface for provisioning
Terraform provider compatibility across KMS/Vault providers remains stable during migration
Dual-write semantics will not introduce transient consistency issues for enrolled apps
implementation_notes: Implement provider abstraction using a single 'key_target' variable with values {aws_kms, gcp_kms, vault, onprem_hsm}
Use separate submodules for provider-specific resources to keep plan outputs minimal
Expose 'rotation_plan' object to drive canary vs immediate rotations; default to canary
Add optional 'drift_detector' resource that creates a scheduled healthcheck and CloudWatch/Stackdriver metrics
CI will run terratest scenarios in ephemeral accounts and a Vault dev cluster to validate idempotence
State handling: recommend remote state with locking and document 'terraform refresh' cadence for operators
